critique.good: All headers and values remain on one line, making rows compact and identifiers easy to follow. The first viewport contains the product identification, variant and quantity fields.
critique.problems: The table requires substantial horizontal scrolling to reach the financial and fulfillment fields. Price begins at the viewport edge, so it is only partially visible.
critique.cause: The 157px SKU and 143px Warehouse columns reserve space for their longest values on one line; together with the 180px Tracking column, they make the table 862px wide.

critique.good: SKU values wrap at hyphens without splitting segments, while headers, amounts and tracking identifiers remain intact. The extra row height keeps each line item visually coherent, and the table is narrower than r0A.
critique.problems: Price is cut off at the right edge of the first viewport. Readers still need to scroll a considerable distance to reach warehouse and tracking information.
critique.cause: The first five columns use 308px, leaving less than the 62px required for Price. The 102px Warehouse and 180px Tracking columns preserve readable fulfillment information but extend the table.

critique.good: Most of the table lies near the viewport, reducing horizontal travel.
critique.problems: Headers, identifiers, colors and monetary amounts break into fragments. Tall rows and uneven text make both cross-row comparison and following a line item difficult.
critique.cause: Widths of 38–51px leave only 17–30px for text in most columns. Even the 50px Tracking column is far narrower than its 159px unbreakable value.

critique.good: The product fields, quantity and price fit within the initial viewport. Headers and compact values stay intact, and the two-line SKU entries give the rows a consistent rhythm.
critique.problems: Readers must scroll a long way to reach tax, total and fulfillment details. The SKU wraps, so comparing the full identifiers takes more effort.
critique.cause: The 99px SKU column permits wrapping at hyphens. The 102px warehouse and 180px tracking columns preserve long words and identifiers but contribute to the 763px overall width.

critique.good: Like r1A, it keeps headers and compact values intact while showing the product fields through price in the initial viewport.
critique.problems: It has the same long horizontal scroll and wrapped SKU values as r1A; it offers no visible alternative.
critique.cause: Its column widths are identical to r1A's.

critique.good: SKUs remain on one line, headers and identifiers stay intact, and the warehouse wraps without splitting words.
critique.problems: The three data rows are tall despite the one-line SKUs, and the first viewport cuts into Price. Readers must scroll substantially to reach fulfillment details.
critique.cause: The 102px Warehouse column wraps its multiword values, setting the row heights; the 157px SKU column consumes space without reducing those heights.

critique.good: Price fits in the first viewport, the SKUs wrap at hyphens, and the warehouse values remain on one line. Headers and tracking identifiers stay intact.
critique.problems: The wrapped SKUs make every data row two lines tall, while the wide warehouse column adds horizontal scrolling without reducing row height.
critique.cause: The 99px SKU column causes the row-height increase; the 143px Warehouse column reserves enough space for one-line values even though the rows already accommodate two lines.

critique.good: Every row is compact and all values remain on one line, making comparisons easy once the relevant columns are visible.
critique.problems: The first viewport cuts into Price, and this is the widest design, requiring the most scrolling to reach tracking.
critique.cause: Both SKU and Warehouse have their full one-line widths, 157px and 143px respectively, in addition to the 180px Tracking column.

r1A.idea: Narrow SKU by 11px from r0B so the first six columns total 359px and Price fits in the initial viewport. Preserve the other readable widths and use natural SKU wrapping.

r1B.idea: Keep Warehouse at its 102px minimum for the intact header and Tracking at 180px for the intact identifier, while allowing warehouse values and SKUs to wrap at natural breaks.

r2A.idea: Give SKU its full one-line width to make identifiers easier to scan and compare. Warehouse values may still wrap; the wider SKU also pushes price beyond the initial viewport and increases scrolling.

r2B.idea: Keep the initial product-through-price view and natural SKU wrapping, while giving warehouse values room on one line. This makes fulfillment locations easier to scan at the cost of additional horizontal scrolling.

r2C.idea: Give both SKU and warehouse their full one-line widths. This tests a compact, single-line row rhythm and easier identifier comparison against the substantially longer horizontal scroll.

r3A.idea: Combine r2B's hyphen-wrapped SKU with r2A's word-wrapped Warehouse. Both can use the same two-line row height, reducing total width to 762px while keeping Price visible initially and tracking identifiers intact.

understanding.purpose: An order or inventory line-item table linking product variants and quantities to prices, warehouse locations and shipment tracking.
understanding.reading: Readers scan each row across to connect a product with its quantity, cost and fulfillment details, and compare quantities and monetary amounts down their columns. On a phone, horizontal scrolling separates the first visible product fields from later fulfillment fields.
groups: ID and SKU identify each line item; Color and Size describe the product variant.
Qty, Price, Tax and Total describe the quantity and financial amounts, which readers compare across rows.
Warehouse and Tracking describe fulfillment and shipment; both are needed to locate or follow an order.
keep_intact: SKU segments and tracking identifiers are most useful when readable without arbitrary character splits.
IDs, quantities, sizes and monetary amounts should stay intact for reliable scanning.
Color names and the Warehouse and Tracking headers should stay intact when space permits.
may_wrap: SKU values may wrap at existing hyphens if the browser permits, though keeping each SKU on one line is easier to scan.
Multiword warehouse values may wrap at word spaces; the resulting row height can also accommodate natural SKU wrapping.

bad.why: Headers, identifiers and numbers split across many lines, making columns and rows difficult to scan. The table still requires horizontal scrolling despite the severe compression.

final.rationale: The preferred designs preserve whole words and numbers while keeping the ID, SKU, product attributes, quantity and price visible in the initial viewport. SKU and warehouse values wrap at available breaks, but the consistent two-line body rows remain easy to follow. Horizontal scrolling is substantial, yet it keeps the later financial and tracking fields legible. The three preferred candidates have identical widths and rendering.

general: Protect the integrity of numbers and identifiers when readers must compare or transcribe them.
Judge the initial viewport and the horizontally scrolled portion together; compression that damages every column can be worse than scrolling.
Consistent row rhythm and clear headers can make moderate wrapping acceptable.
specific: The long tracking values set a substantial minimum width for the final column.
A narrower SKU column brings price into the initial viewport while allowing SKU values to wrap at breaks.
Widening both SKU and warehouse produces compact single-line rows, but increases the horizontal distance readers must scroll.

final.tradeoffs: r2C keeps every value on one line and produces more compact rows, at the cost of a wider table and price falling outside the initial viewport. The preferred designs favor earlier access to price and less horizontal scrolling while accepting wrapped SKU and warehouse values.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative estimates around the preferred widths, not browser-verified thresholds; their combined effect on the viewport boundary may matter. A designer could reasonably prefer r2C if uninterrupted identifier scanning matters more than seeing price immediately.

A.why: The visible columns are clear and the SKUs stay intact, but Price begins beyond the viewport, so comparison requires early horizontal scrolling.

B.why: Headers, SKUs, values and tracking identifiers break into narrow vertical fragments, making rows and columns very difficult to scan.

C.why: Most visible fields are legible, but each SKU occupies four lines, weakening row rhythm and making identifiers harder to compare.

D.why: Many headers, numbers and identifiers split across lines; the resulting tall rows are difficult to read and compare.

E.why: The visible rows are compact, with SKUs breaking at hyphens, but the Price values sit against the viewport edge and require scrolling to see comfortably.

F.why: The visible rows have a compact rhythm, SKUs break at hyphens, and complete Price values fit within the viewport.

reviews.unsure: The supplied views show only the left portion of each table, so the widths and readability of later columns, especially Warehouse and Tracking, cannot be fully assessed.

A.why: The SKU wraps at hyphens and rows remain easy to follow, but Price is cut by the viewport edge, so its values require scrolling to read.

B.why: SKU wraps into two readable lines, and the first view includes complete values through Price. Tax begins at the edge, signalling more columns to the right.

C.why: Nearly every header and many values split into isolated letters or digits. The very tall rows make comparison difficult, while Tracking still extends beyond the viewport.

D.why: The first view reaches Tax and keeps the short values intact, but the narrow SKU column breaks each identifier across four lines, making rows taller and identifiers harder to scan.

E.why: The compressed columns fragment headers, prices, colours and identifiers across many lines. Despite the dense layout, the rightmost content still requires scrolling.

F.why: Complete SKUs make the rows compact and identifiers easy to compare, but the first view stops at the start of Price, leaving more of the table to horizontal scrolling.

reviews.unsure: The supplied views show only portions of the wider layouts, so the readability and width of columns farther to the right cannot be assessed fully. F may be preferable if keeping each SKU on one line is especially important.
